brief.headline: Push for a 35% price reduction to close the ₹23.53/KG gap to the India export benchmark of ₹42.95/KG, leveraging our 1.38% revenue share and three credible alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Demand price reduction from ₹66.48/KG to match or beat the India export unit value of ₹42.95/KG for Dextrose.
priceAsk.target: ₹42.95/KG (India export unit value from UN Comtrade)
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay ₹66.48/KG — 55% above the market line of ₹42.95/KG. This gap is indefensible when export-grade material trades at ₹42.95/KG and we have multiple alternate suppliers including Gulshan Polyols, Sanstar, and Roquette India ready to quote.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment in exchange for a 2–3% cash discount, citing their high debt load.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹1.24 Cr (working capital currently locked; freeing it funds the discount and improves their cash flow)

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji's net margin is a razor-thin 1.1% and EBITDA margin is 4.9%, so they have limited room to absorb deep cuts — but their debt-to-equity of 2.37x means cash is king. Our ₹15.03 Cr annual spend represents 1.38% of their ₹1087.88 Cr revenue, making us a meaningful customer they cannot afford to lose. Their D (17/100) health score signals stress, so frame the ask as a partnership to stabilize volume in exchange for competitive pricing. Offer faster payment to ease their working-capital squeeze, but anchor hard on the ₹42.95/KG market line — we have five credible alternates and no switching cost.

evidence.point: We pay ₹66.48/KG for Dextrose, 55% above the India export benchmark.
Our ₹15.03 Cr annual spend is 1.38% of Sayaji's ₹1087.88 Cr revenue — a material customer relationship.
Sayaji's net margin is only 1.1% and EBITDA margin is 4.9%, limiting their ability to defend high pricing.
Their debt-to-equity ratio is 2.37x, signaling cash-flow pressure and openness to faster payment in exchange for price relief.
Moving to immediate payment would free ₹1.24 Cr of our working capital, funding a discount while easing their cash cycle.
Their financial health score is D (17/100), underscoring the need to secure volume and improve terms to stabilize operations.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate to Sayaji with C health score.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) — growing capacity with B health score, stronger financials than Sayaji.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major Roquette — pharma-grade dextrose/excipients; premium, very reliable, de-risking supply continuity concerns.

risks: Sayaji's 1.1% net margin and D (17/100) health score mean aggressive price pressure could destabilize supply — balance the ask with volume commitment and faster payment to keep them viable.
We currently pay ₹66.48/KG with no gap to our own best price, so we lack internal benchmarking leverage — rely entirely on the ₹42.95/KG export market line and alternate quotes to justify the ask.

Their 2.37x debt-to-equity and thin margins may limit their ability to cut price deeply; if they refuse, pivot to payment terms (cash discount for faster payment) and lock in a commitment to revisit pricing quarterly against the export benchmark.

Our 1.38% share of their revenue gives us leverage, but not dominance — if we walk, they lose a meaningful customer but won't collapse; ensure alternates are pre-qualified before issuing an ultimatum.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but at ₹66.48/KG we're paying 55% over the ₹42.95/KG India export benchmark for Dextrose — let's work together to close that gap so we can commit our full ₹15 Cr annual volume to you.
